text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 1.6% today, closing a two-week slide of 7.4%. The drop follows a sharp pullback from peaks hit mid-week (around $415), and comes as crude oil prices have drifted lower—US oil sits at $89.62 a barrel, down from levels that likely supported refiner margins earlier this month. Refineries are running at 95.2% capacity, a healthy utilization rate, but the recent cooling in oil prices and broader weakness in energy stocks over the past week appear to be weighing on the company's valuation.

The timing also reflects some softening in demand signals: heating oil prices remain elevated from last year's levels, but rising shipping costs and cautious retail inventory planning suggest softer overall transportation fuel demand heading into the winter period. Meanwhile, geopolitical risk in the Middle East (the Iran-carrier tensions) could theoretically support crude prices, but hasn't prevented the recent decline—indicating traders may be more focused on near-term demand weakness than supply disruption fears at the moment.
